SOURCE = IndependentSet

Instance: {"n": n, "edges": [[u, v], ...], "k": k}
  * Vertices are 0..n-1. Edges are undirected pairs [u, v] with u != v;
    [u, v] and [v, u] are the same edge and may not both appear.
  * k is any integer.

Yes iff the graph has an independent set of AT LEAST k vertices: k
vertices with no edge between any two of them.

Edge cases: k <= 0 is always yes. k > n is always no. With no edges,
every set of vertices is independent.

TARGET = Clique
Clique.

Instance: {"n": n, "edges": [[u, v], ...], "k": k}

  * k is any integer.

edge between every two of them.

Edge cases: k <= 0 is always yes. k = 1 is yes whenever n >= 1. k > n is
always no.

The answer to the returned instance must be yes exactly when the answer to the input instance is yes, and reduce must run in polynomial time. Do not call the brute-force solvers inside reduce.

{"command":"cd /tmp/reduction-0p154a6h && cat > reduce.py <<'EOF'
"""Polynomial-time reduction from Independent Set to Clique.

An independent set in a graph G is exactly a clique in the complement
graph of G.  So the reduction keeps n and k unchanged and replaces the
edge set by its complement on the same vertex set.

Edge cases:
  * k <= 0 : yes for the source, and the target instance also has k <= 0,
             so it is yes as well.
  * k > n  : no for the source, and the target instance has the same n and
             k, so it is no as well.
  * n == 0 : the complement is empty and k > 0 is impossible, matching the
             source (only k <= 0 can be yes).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from itertools import combinations


def reduce(instance):
    """Map an Independent Set instance to a Clique instance.

    The returned graph is the complement of the input graph; n and k are
    unchanged.
    """
    n = instance["n"]
    k = instance["k"]

    # Canonicalise the existing edges as unordered pairs so that a reversed
    # representation [v, u] is treated the same as [u, v].
    present = set()
    for u, v in instance["edges"]:
        present.add((u, v) if u < v else (v, u))

    complement_edges = [
        [u, v] for u, v in combinations(range(n), 2) if (u, v) not in present
    ]

    return {"n": n, "edges": complement_edges, "k": k}
EOF

"""Polynomial-time reduction from Independent Set to Clique.

An independent set in a graph G is exactly a clique in the complement
graph of G.  So the reduction keeps n and k unchanged and replaces the
edge set by its complement on the same vertex set.

Edge cases:
  * k <= 0 : yes for the source, and the target instance also has k <= 0,
             so it is yes as well.
  * k > n  : no for the source, and the target instance has the same n and
             k, so it is no as well.
  * n == 0 : the complement is empty and k > 0 is impossible, matching the
             source (only k <= 0 can be yes).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from itertools import combinations


def reduce(instance):
    """Map an Independent Set instance to a Clique instance.

    The returned graph is the complement of the input graph; n and k are
    unchanged.
    """
    n = instance["n"]
    k = instance["k"]

    # Canonicalise the existing edges as unordered pairs so that a reversed
    # representation [v, u] is treated the same as [u, v].
    present = set()
    for u, v in instance["edges"]:
        present.add((u, v) if u < v else (v, u))

    complement_edges = [
        [u, v] for u, v in combinations(range(n), 2) if (u, v) not in present
    ]

    return {"n": n, "edges": complement_edges, "k": k}
